blocks.content: Human rights relate to life, liberty, equality and dignity of the individual guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in the International Covenants.

items: Section 2(1)(d) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 is frequently tested regarding the legal definition of human rights in India.
Human Rights Day is observed worldwide on 10th December to commemorate the adoption of the UDHR in 1948.
Distinguish between Fundamental Rights (guaranteed by the Constitution) and broader Human Rights (universal standards).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Human rights are inherent rights possessed by all human beings, irrespective of nationality, sex, race, religion, or language.
Section 2(1)(d) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 defines human rights as rights relating to life, liberty, equality, and dignity.
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the UN General Assembly on December 10, 1948.
Fundamental Rights under Part III of the Indian Constitution represent judicially enforceable civil and political human rights.
